Meow Star Map·Full walkthrough

Meow Star Map is a desktop app that helps you manage your Infinity Nikki screenshots. It can:

This guide is written for every player — no computer expertise needed.
All screenshots come from the app actually running on a PC (version 2.5.0-beta, Windows).
Follow the chapters step by step: from the very first launch to advanced workflows, each action has its own page.

🧭 First-time path

New here? Walk this path once and you will cover the whole flow from installing to sharing.

1Install2Main window3Browse4Organise5Edit6Share

✨ What the app does

  • 🔍 Finds automatically the photos and videos the game saves on your PC and turns them into a browsable album;
  • 🖼️ Offers grid, timeline, masonry and more ways to browse, with filters by date, rating and type, plus search;
  • ✏️ Built-in editing: brightness, filters, watermarks — no other editor needed;
  • 🎮 Game-specific extras: outfit tagging, a gacha history (Resonance Log) and in-game camera settings;
  • 🧹 Finds duplicate and similar photos so you can reclaim disk space in one click;
  • 📤 One-click share to WeChat / QQ, or WiFi share straight to your phone;
  • 🗑️ Two-layer trash protection so deleted photos can come back.

🗂 Module entries

The guide has three levels: overview → section page (index and summary) → detail page (steps, examples, caveats). Click a card to enter, or jump anywhere with the search box at the top.

m1p1.desc: Get the installer from GitHub Releases and install it like any other app.
m1p1.html:
1. Open the project's GitHub Releases page (or the download link the author lists on Douyin / Bilibili);
  2. Download the package named something like MeowStarMap-Setup-2.5.0-beta.exe;
  3. Double-click it and click “Next” as you would for any installer;
  4. When it finishes, the Meow Star Map icon appears on your desktop and in the Start menu.
m1p1.lead: Three minutes to install, then the Meow Star Map icon appears on your desktop.
m1p1.text: Download and install Get the installer from GitHub Releases and install it like any other app. Three minutes to install. Open GitHub Releases, download MeowStarMap-Setup, double-click and follow the wizard.
m1p1.title: Download and install

m1p2.desc: Empty library on first launch? The app finds the game and scans your photos automatically.
m1p2.html:
On first launch the library is empty and shows “No media yet”:

{{img1}}

No need to configure anything — a few seconds after launch the app automatically finds the installed Infinity Nikki, locates the folder where the game saves photos and starts scanning. When it finishes, all your game photos appear in the library.
m1p2.lead: No manual setup: a few seconds after launch the photos appear by themselves.
m1p2.text: First launch it looks for your game photos Empty library on first launch? The app finds the game and scans your photos automatically. It locates Infinity Nikki and its photo folder.
m1p2.title: First launch: it looks for your game photos

m1p3.desc: Three areas: left menu, top toolbar, content area — plus multi-profile switching.
m1p3.html:
When the app opens you land on the main “Library” page:

{{img1}}

The window has three areas:

  • Left menu: entries for the nine sections — Library, Screenshots, Favourites, Resonance Log, Cache, Categories, Duplicates, Trash, Settings;
  • Top toolbar: type filter (all / images / videos), rating, date, sort order, search box, plus import, view switch and scan buttons;
  • Content area: the photos live here. The counts of photos and videos sit in the bottom-left corner.

The “library overview” screenshot above boxes all three areas — compare it once and you are familiar.

💡 Tip: the “All profiles” dropdown at the top left switches character profiles (separated by in-game UID). If you play several accounts, each one is managed separately, and “All profiles” shows them together.
m1p3.lead: Use the “library overview” screenshot to learn the nine section entries.
m1p3.text: Getting to know the main window Three areas: left menu, top toolbar, content area plus multi-profile switching. Library, screenshots, favourites, resonance log, cache, categories, duplicates, trash, settings.
m1p3.title: Getting to know the main window

m1p4.desc: Incremental scan, auto-locate and manual folder — even if the game lives somewhere unusual.
m1p4.html:
Three scanning modes

Day to day, the app scans for new photos on every launch — you do not need to do anything. To scan manually, click the small arrow next to the scan button and pick a mode.

Nothing found? Pick the folder yourself

If the automatic scan finds nothing (for example the game is installed in an unusual place), point the app at it manually:

  1. Click the small arrow next to the scan button on the right of the toolbar to open the scan menu;

{{img1}}

  1. The menu offers three modes:
    • Incremental scan (new files only): finds only newly captured photos and is fast — recommended for daily use;
    • Auto-locate the game folder: asks the app to try finding the game again;
    • Choose a folder: pick it yourself — if the game is installed somewhere unusual, choose this, then select the game's X6Game\Saved\GamePlayPhotos folder (or any folder where you keep photos) and click “Select folder”.
  2. Progress shows in the bottom-right corner while scanning; when it finishes the photos appear in the library.
💡 Tip: “Scan on launch” is on by default, so every start looks for new photos without manual work. You can change it in Settings → General → Startup behaviour.
m1p4.lead: If the automatic scan finds nothing, point the app at the GamePlayPhotos folder.
m1p4.text: Scanning modes and picking a folder yourself Incremental scan, auto-locate and manual folder even if the game lives somewhere unusual. GamePlayPhotos folder, scan menu, auto-locate.
m1p4.title: Scanning modes and picking a folder yourself

m1p5.desc: Three steps: pick a folder, tick files, set rules. The source folder is never modified.
m1p5.html:
Beyond the game folder, you can copy images and videos from any folder on your PC into the app:

  1. Click the Import button on the left of the toolbar (the first icon) to open the wizard;

{{img1}}

  1. Step 1: click “Browse” and choose the folder that holds the photos;
  2. Step 2: preview the files and tick the ones you want;
  3. Step 3: set the import rules (target folder, naming, what to do about duplicates) and start the import.

Afterwards those photos appear in the library alongside the game photos.

💡 Tip: import copies files — nothing in the original folder is moved or changed, so it is safe.
m1p5.lead: Pull images and videos from any folder into one managed library.
m1p5.text: Import photos from other folders (import wizard) Three steps pick a folder, tick files, set rules. The source folder is never modified. Copies images and videos into the library.
m1p5.title: Import photos from other folders (import wizard)

m2p1.desc: Grid, list, timeline and masonry — switch with one click.
m2p1.html:
The view buttons sit in the middle of the toolbar — one click switches:

  • Grid (default): an even grid of tiles;
  • List: one photo per row with more details;
  • Timeline: grouped by date, handy for recalling what you shot on a given day;
  • Masonry: photos keep their original proportions, which feels better for larger previews.

{{img1}}

{{img2}}
m2p1.lead: The view buttons in the middle of the toolbar change how photos are laid out.
m2p1.text: Another layout four gallery views Grid, list, timeline and masonry switch with one click. Timeline groups by date, masonry keeps original proportions.
m2p1.title: Another layout: four gallery views

m2p2.desc: Filter by type, rating and date, sort by several columns, search keywords live.
m2p2.html:
Filter: find the right photos fast

The toolbar offers several filters that can be combined:

  • Type: all / images / videos;
  • Rating: only rated photos (for example “3 stars and up”);

{{img1}}

  • Date: pick a start and end date to see only that period;
  • Missing only / corrupted only: check whether any file has a problem (moved by hand, broken file).

Sorting

The row of buttons “date / name / size / resolution / rating” sorts the library; click once to sort by it and again to flip between descending and ascending.

Search

Type a keyword and the app searches as you type across file names, tags, outfits, scenes and notes. For example, type part of a file name and the matching photos appear at once:

{{img2}}
m2p2.lead: Find the few photos you want among thousands.
m2p2.text: Filtering, sorting and search Filter by type, rating and date, sort by several columns, search keywords live. Missing only, corrupted only, sort order, search as you type.
m2p2.title: Filtering, sorting and search

m2p3.desc: Group automatically by album type, outfit, scene or time of day.
m2p3.html:
Pressing “Smart grouping” groups photos automatically by album type / type / outfit / scene / time of day. The groups appear under the left menu; pick one to see only that group:

{{img1}}
m2p3.lead: Press “Smart grouping” and pick a group from the left.
m2p3.text: Smart grouping Group automatically by album type, outfit, scene or time of day. Groups appear under the left menu.
m2p3.title: Smart grouping

m2p4.desc: Click to go full screen, page with the keyboard, read camera settings, even play a slideshow.
m2p4.html:
Full-screen viewing

Click any photo to open it full screen:

{{img1}}

In full screen you can:

  • Press ← / → or click the side arrows to move between photos;
  • Click the star button at the bottom right to favourite it; click info to see the details — photos taken in game also show the in-game camera settings (aperture, focal length, lighting, filter and so on);
  • Press Esc or click the × at the top right to return to the library.

{{img2}}

Slideshow

In full screen, press the play button at the top and the photos advance automatically. The interval button next to it (for example “3s”) sets how long each photo stays (1/2/3/5/8 seconds):

{{img3}}
m2p4.lead: Everything about full-screen viewing and playback.
m2p4.text: Full screen and slideshow Click to go full screen, page with the keyboard, read camera settings, even play a slideshow. Aperture, focal length, lighting, filter, interval.
m2p4.title: Full screen and slideshow

m2p5.desc: Videos live beside photos: duration badge, dedicated filter, full-screen playback.
m2p5.html:
Videos recorded in game appear in the library beside photos, with a duration badge in the bottom-right corner of the thumbnail. Use the video filter at the top to see only videos:

{{img1}}

Click a video to play it full screen. Videos support the same management features as photos: favourites, ratings, tags, sharing and export.

⚠️ Note: in this beta, the “Edit” entry for videos is not open yet (the right-click “Edit” item is greyed out for videos). This is expected; later versions will add trimming, speed changes and format conversion.
m2p5.lead: How recorded videos are shown and managed.
m2p5.text: Working with game videos Videos live beside photos duration badge, dedicated filter, full-screen playback. Editing is not available for videos yet.
m2p5.title: Working with game videos

m2p6.desc: Three sections grouped automatically by source.
m2p6.html:
The sidebar has three more sections, grouped automatically by source:

  • Screenshots: images captured with the in-game screenshot key;

{{img1}}

  • Favourites: every starred photo;

{{img2}}

  • Cache: wallpapers and promo art downloaded by the game launcher. Looking for an official wallpaper for your desktop? Browse here:

{{img3}}

m3p1.desc: Rate at the bottom of the detail page, favourite from the side panel.
m3p1.html:
Rating

The detail page has five stars at the bottom; click as many as you want to score. Rated photos can be found quickly with the rating filter.

Favourites

The info panel on the right of the detail page has a “Favourite” switch; hovering a thumbnail in the library also reveals a star button. Starred photos are collected in the “Favourites” section.
m3p1.lead: Two clicks to mark your best photos.
m3p1.text: Rating and favourites Rate at the bottom of the detail page, favourite from the side panel. Five stars, rating filter, star button on hover.
m3p1.title: Rating and favourites

m3p2.desc: Custom tags plus 35 built-in outfit presets that feed search and grouping.
m3p2.html:
Tags

Press the tag button at the top to add custom tags (common ones such as scenery, character and story are one click away). Searching the tag name later finds that batch of photos.

{{img1}}

Outfit marking: what is the character wearing?

Find “Outfit” on the right of the detail page, click Add, then type the outfit name or pick one of the 35 built-in presets from the list and click “Save”:

{{img2}}

Marked photos can be browsed by outfit with “Smart grouping → Outfit”, and searching the outfit name finds them instantly.
m3p2.lead: Tell the app what a photo is wearing.
m3p2.text: Tags and outfit marking Custom tags plus 35 built-in outfit presets that feed search and grouping. Smart grouping by outfit.
m3p2.title: Tags and outfit marking

m3p3.desc: The right-click menu collects common actions; undo from the toast.
m3p3.html:
Right-click menu: the everyday actions

Right-click any photo in the library to open the menu: open, edit, save as, export, copy to, move to, rename, share, favourite, delete, properties:

{{img1}}

Slipped up? Undo

After moving, deleting or renaming, the toast that appears offers undo, restoring the photo exactly as before.
m3p3.lead: Everyday actions live in the right-click menu, and slip-ups are reversible.
m3p3.text: Right-click menu and global undo The right-click menu collects common actions; undo from the toast. Open, edit, save as, export, copy to, move to, rename, share.
m3p3.title: Right-click menu and global undo

m3p4.desc: Ctrl / Shift multi-select, then delete, export, rename or watermark in one go.
m3p4.html:
Selecting several photos

  • Ctrl + click: toggle one photo (non-adjacent selections work);
  • Shift + click: select the range between two clicks;
  • Once selected, “Select all / invert” buttons appear at the bottom.

{{img1}}

What the batch bar can do

When photos are selected a row of buttons appears at the bottom:

ButtonWhat it does
DeleteMoves the selected photos to the app trash (recoverable)
ExportChoose a folder and copy the photos out
Export to defaultExports straight to your configured default folder (set in Settings → General → Export workflow)
MoveMoves photos to another folder
WatermarkApplies one watermark to every selected photo
RenameBatch rename by template (date, sequence, outfit and so on)
Move to profileMoves photos under another UID profile

Press × on the right to clear the selection when you are done.
m3p4.lead: The full button table for working on many photos at once.
m3p4.text: Batch actions handle a pile at once Ctrl / Shift multi-select, then delete, export, rename or watermark in one go. Export to default, move to profile, wifi share.
m3p4.title: Batch actions: handle a pile at once

m3p5.desc: Build your own category tree, file photos into it; built-in scene categories group automatically.
m3p5.html:
The “Categories” section lets you build your own classification:

{{img1}}

  • New category: set name, colour and icon, and nest it under another category to build levels (for example “Fields” and “Snow peaks” under “Landscape”);
  • File photos: press “Assign media” on a category, search and tick photos; you can also drag a photo from the library onto a category;
  • The app also ships in-game scene categories (thumbnails, screenshots, travel journal, world tour and more) that group photos by source automatically;
  • Scene time of day: in Settings → Scanning → Scan options press “Analyse now” and the app works out whether each photo is day, morning, dusk or night, so you can filter by time of day afterwards.
💡 Tip: deleting a custom category never deletes the photos inside it.
m3p5.text: Category management Build your own category tree, file photos into it; built-in scene categories group automatically. New category, assign media, scene categories, scene time of day.
m3p5.title: Category management

m4p4.desc: Hold to compare, split-view compare; saving backs up the original; shortcut table.
m4p4.html:
Comparing with the original

Want to know how much you changed? Two ways:

  • Hold the “Compare” button: the original shows while held, the edit returns when released;
  • Split view: original on one side, edit on the other.

{{img1}}

Saving and exporting

  • Save: writes the edit back to the photo. Don't worry — the original file is backed up automatically and can be restored;
  • Save as: keeps the original and writes the edit to a new file;
  • Export with settings: writes a copy that carries the edit parameters, so they can be restored into the editor later;
  • Apply to selection: applies the current settings to the other selected photos in one go.

The top bar also has undo / redo / reset.

Common shortcuts

ShortcutAction
Ctrl + SSave
Ctrl + Z / Ctrl + YUndo / redo

m6p1.desc: Exact duplicates plus similar detection, highlighted keepers, one-click policies.
m6p1.html:
Burst shots and repeated exports easily create duplicates. Open the “Duplicates” section and the app starts detecting automatically:

{{img1}}

  • Exact duplicates: files with identical content (say, the same photo saved twice);
  • Similar detection: goes further and finds photos of the same scene with only minor differences; the strictness is adjustable;

{{img2}}

In each group the app highlights the one worth keeping (judged by sharpness, size and capture time). You can:

  • Use the one-click policies at the top: keep the best quality / newest / largest / favourites;
  • Or tick what to delete group by group and press “Move to trash” (recoverable);
  • Mark duplicates: tag duplicates so the library hides them automatically (turn on “Show duplicates” when you want to see them).
💡 Tip: everything goes through the trash first — no file is deleted outright.
m6p1.lead: Find duplicates and reclaim disk space.
m6p1.text: Cleaning up duplicate photos Exact duplicates plus similar detection, highlighted keepers, one-click policies. Keep best quality, newest, largest, favourites, mark duplicates.
m6p1.title: Cleaning up duplicate photos

m6p2.desc: App trash plus the system recycle bin — two chances to recover.
m6p2.html:
When you delete a photo (right-click, batch delete, duplicate cleanup) it first goes to the app's own trash — the file stays where it is and can be restored at any time:

{{img1}}

  • Restore: tick the items and press “Restore” to bring them back into the library;
  • Delete permanently / empty trash: only this step sends the file to the system recycle bin (with one more confirmation).

So a mistaken delete has two safety nets: the app trash, and then the system recycle bin.

⚠️ Caution: “Delete permanently” in the right-click menu skips the trash. It asks for confirmation, but use it carefully.
m6p2.lead: Deleted photos land here first and can come back.
m6p2.text: Trash two layers of safety App trash plus the system recycle bin two chances to recover. Restore, empty trash, delete permanently.
m6p2.title: Trash: two layers of safety

m7p1.desc: Photos go to the clipboard; the app checks WeChat / QQ and you paste.
m7p1.html:
Select photos (a single photo can use the right-click “Share”), press Share and choose “Share to WeChat / Share to QQ / Share to vivo office suite” from the menu:

{{img1}}

The app puts the photos on the clipboard and checks whether the target app is running: if it is, you are told to press Ctrl + V to send; if not, you are asked to open it first.

m7p2.desc: LAN sharing: same WiFi, enter the PIN, view and download.
m7p2.html:
Want the photos on your phone? Select them and press WiFi share to start a LAN share:

{{img1}}

  1. Connect the phone and the PC to the same WiFi;
  2. Open the address shown on screen in the phone browser;
  3. Enter the PIN shown on screen, then view and download the photos on the phone.

The share counts down and stops by itself, and “Stop sharing” works at any time. The address and PIN may change every time — trust what the screen shows.
m7p2.lead: No cable — grab photos on your phone.
m7p2.text: WiFi share download straight to your phone LAN sharing same WiFi, enter the PIN, view and download. Address and PIN shown on screen.
m7p2.title: WiFi share: download straight to your phone

m8p5.desc: 7-day automatic backups, cache limits, what clearing data does.
m8p5.html:
• Database backup: the album database is backed up automatically every 7 days (the latest 5 kept), and “Back up now” runs one immediately; back up before switching computers or reinstalling;

{{img1}}

  • Cache: thumbnail cache size and cleanup. Once a limit is set, the least recently viewed thumbnails are cleaned automatically to free space — originals are untouched;

{{img2}}

  • Clear data: “Clean missing records” removes stale index entries only; “Clear local data” empties the album records and tags (photo files on disk are not touched), which suits a fresh rescan.
m8p5.lead: Read this before switching PCs or reinstalling.

m9p1.desc: Ten most common questions: empty library, permissions, recovery, blank screen, migration.
m9p1.html:
Q1: the library is empty after launch. The app scans automatically a few seconds after start. If nothing appears: click the small arrow next to the scan button → “Choose a folder” and pick the game's GamePlayPhotos folder or wherever you keep photos (see Scanning modes).

Q2: “permission denied (E003)” while scanning. The app cannot read the game folder. Go to Settings → Scanning → Manual fallback scan, press “Restart as administrator” and scan again.

Q3: the file is on disk but missing from the library. It was probably moved. Use “Missing only” in the library to find stale records, put the file back and rescan; records you no longer want can be removed with Settings → Data management → Clean missing records.

Q4: I deleted a photo by mistake. Open the Trash section and restore it. Even after a permanent delete the system recycle bin still has a copy.

Q5: I regret an edit. Press Ctrl + Z in the editor, or “Reset” to drop every adjustment; quitting without saving leaves the original alone. Saved photos also keep an automatic backup of the original file.

Q6: the app crashes or goes blank. Go to Settings → General → Startup, turn off “GPU hardware acceleration” and restart. The app also recovers automatically after a crash. More logs are available under Settings → Logs and diagnostics.

Q7: moving to a new PC. Old PC: Settings → Data management → Database backup → Back up now. On the new PC, install the app and restore that backup from the same page (copy the photo files yourself).

Q8: the thumbnail cache is huge. Settings → Data management → Cache offers one-click cleanup and an automatic limit; only thumbnails are affected.

Q9: the interface is in English — how do I switch back to Chinese? Settings → General → Language, pick “Simplified Chinese” and it applies immediately.

Q10: WeChat/QQ share does nothing. Sharing puts photos on the clipboard, so the target app must be running: open WeChat or QQ first, press Share in the app, then paste with Ctrl + V in the chat window.
m9p1.lead: Check the index first, jump straight to the answer.
